memories.content: Specify the order and recipients for reporting serious discomfort during the study.
Field staff rely on a pre-defined contact sequence when serious discomfort is reported.
Establish criteria for halting the use of a design alternative if recurring severe errors appear during formative evaluation.
Do not include a design alternative halted for safety reasons in subsequent evaluation iterations without modification.
Even in controlled environments, delayed prototype recovery procedures increase session interruption time and alter data collection conditions for the same task.
Do not change names referring to the same user roles, system functions, or operational stages midway.
Use abbreviations only for long recurring terms in a two-page proposal.
Present the full term and abbreviation together when using an abbreviation for the first time.
Refer to participants based on the roles they perform in the study rather than their status.
Reviewers from different subfields find it difficult to infer an abbreviation from context alone when it is not defined at first use.
When introducing an operational role for the first time, define both the decisions it can make and the actions it performs.
Individuals holding identical job titles may possess different system modification privileges and data access rights depending on their deployment site.
The user tends to group distinct field roles under the single label “user.”

analysis.overview: The frames address separate concerns. The reference covers safety escalation, stopping unsafe alternatives, and prototype recovery effects; the compared frame covers consistent role terminology, abbreviation practices, participant labeling, role definitions, and site-dependent permissions. No scope-aligned overlap or conflict is present.

relations.reason: The two reference memories state complementary parts of one one-sided operational requirement: defining the contact order and relying on it in the field.
relations.summary: Serious discomfort reports require a predefined reporting sequence with specified recipients.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful reference-only stopping rule with no corresponding compared-side claim.
relations.summary: Formative evaluation should have criteria for halting a design alternative when severe errors recur.

relations.reason: This reference-only restriction governs subsequent reuse rather than the initial halting decision and has no compared-side counterpart.
relations.summary: A design alternative halted for safety reasons must be modified before later evaluation.

relations.reason: This is a standalone reference-only observation about evaluation conditions with no compared-side counterpart.
relations.summary: Delayed prototype recovery increases interruptions and changes data-collection conditions even in controlled settings.

relations.reason: This compared-only naming policy has no scope-aligned reference-side claim.
relations.summary: Names for the same roles, functions, and operational stages should remain consistent throughout a document.

relations.reason: This compared-only criterion determines when abbreviations are worthwhile and has no reference-side counterpart.
relations.summary: In a two-page proposal, abbreviations should be reserved for long terms that recur.

relations.reason: The compared memories split one underlying claim into a first-use rule and its audience-based rationale; the reference has no counterpart.
relations.summary: An abbreviation should be paired with its full term at first use because context alone may not serve reviewers across subfields.

relations.reason: The compared memories express the role-based labeling policy and the observed tendency it addresses; no reference-side claim covers participant naming.
relations.summary: Participants should be labeled by their study roles rather than collapsed into status-based or generic user labels.

relations.reason: This compared-only role-definition requirement has no corresponding reference-side claim.
relations.summary: A newly introduced operational role should be defined by both its decision authority and its performed actions.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful compared-only scope observation about site-dependent authority, not merely a restatement of how roles should be introduced.
relations.summary: People with the same job title may have different modification privileges and data-access rights across deployment sites.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame sets terminology and abbreviation practices, favors role-specific participant labels, requires operational-role definitions, and notes site-dependent permissions.
reports.reference_only: The reference specifies serious-discomfort escalation, safety-based stopping and reuse rules, and the effects of delayed prototype recovery.
